walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems & Ecology — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems & Ecology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems & Ecology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Typical energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels:
What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Stopping all development immediately.
They are the same problem.

mcqs.q: How does the Brundtland Report define sustainable development?
options: About 50 percent.
Stopping all development immediately.
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
Environmental protection at all costs.

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: About 50 percent.
Stopping all development immediately.
100 percent (everything transfers).
About 10 percent.
